title: Least-Privilege Quarterly Runbook and SIEM Ingest Notes
body:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook describes the operational steps, automation tasks, SIEM export mapping, and validation checks we run for quarterly least-privilege access certification across Redwood Inference. It is focused on RBAC v2 roles, how we capture evidence snapshots, and how exported audit logs are consumed in our SIEM for exception triage. This is intended as an operational playbook for Security and Platform teams executing the quarterly access review.

High-level goals:
- Verify that role assignments match business need and revoke stale access.
- Produce tamper-evident evidence packages for auditors (snapshots, hashes, and audit log slices).
- Feed relevant audit events into SIEM with consistent field mapping for detection and reporting.
- Automate majority of evidence collection to minimize manual errors.

Pre-run checklist (T minus 7 days)
- Confirm quarter window and notify all app owners and approvers. (owner: security-ops)
- Open JIRA-SEC-987 (linked) with schedule and owners.
- Ensure the latest RBAC v2 role definitions are tagged in GitHub (repo: infra/rbac-roles, branch: main).
- Confirm access-evidence-snap tool is at tag v1.3.2 and the S3 evidence bucket (s3://redwood-compliance-evidence) has write retention policy configured.
- Validate SIEM ingest pipeline (splunk/hec or elastic ingest) is green by running a test event.

Roles and responsibilities
- Security-ops: run the recertification automation, coordinate approvers, escalate exceptions.
- Platform: provide RBAC v2 exports and owner mappings, support snapshot tool.
- App owners: review and approve/revoke access for their services.
- Compliance: spot-check evidence packages and confirm immutability.

Automated evidence collection (recommended flow)
1) RBAC v2 role export
   - Run: tools/export-rbac-v2.sh --output=rbac-export-{{quarter}}.json
   - Output fields: principal_id, principal_type, role_id, role_name, scope (org/team/service), binding_id, binding_created_at
   - Save copy to evidence staging: s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/{{quarter}}/rbac-export.json

2) Active-principals snapshot
   - Run: tools/list-active-principals --since={{quarter_start}} --until={{quarter_end}} > active-principals.csv
   - Fields: principal_id, email, last_seen, last_token_issue, linked_roles

3) Permission delta heuristic
   - Script: tools/compute-role-delta.rb rbac-export.json previous-rbac.json -> delta-report.csv
   - Flag changes where (new role grants more than N perms) or (role moved to broader scope).

4) Audit log slice (evidence window)
   - Query gateway audit log store for the quarter window and for events relevant to access: role.bind, role.unbind, token.issue, token.revoke, vault.kms-access, console.login, api.key.create.
   - Example ES query (pseudo): {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "2024-10-01", "lte": "2024-12-31"}}, "terms": {"event.type": ["role.bind", "role.unbind", "token.issue", "token.revoke"]}}
   - Save as audit-slice-{{quarter}}.ndjson and push to evidence bucket.

SIEM export and field mapping notes
- Our SIEM requires consistent event fields. When exporting audit logs from the gateway runtime, ensure the following schema mapping (these are the canonical field names we expect in Splunk/Elastic):

  source_event_time -> @timestamp
  actor.id -> principal_id
  actor.email -> principal_email
  actor.type -> principal_type
  action -> event.action (role.bind, role.unbind, token.issue, etc.)
  resource.type -> resource_type (role, service_account, key)
  resource.id -> resource_id
  resource.scope -> resource_scope
  outcome -> event.outcome (success|failure)
  request.id -> request_id
  trace.id -> trace_id

- SIEM ingestion tips:
  - Add a pipeline transform that drops internal debug events (event.action == "debug.*").
  - Normalize timestamp to UTC at parse time.
  - Add enrichment: map principal_id -> HR identifier using the people service API to get manager and team for triage.

Recommended Splunk/Elastic queries for triage
- Find bindings created without an owner mapping:
  - Splunk: index=audits event.action=role.bind NOT resource.owner_id=* | table @timestamp principal_email role_name resource_scope
- Find role grants that expanded scope from team -> org in the quarter:
  - ES DSL: see compute-role-delta output or use KQL: event.action:role.bind and resource_scope:org and previous_scope:team
- Token issues outside regular hours (possible automation keys):
  - Splunk: index=audits event.action=token.issue | eval hour=strftime(_time, "%H") | where hour < 7 OR hour > 19 | table _time principal_email request_id

Approval workflow (UI + evidence attachments)
- For each binding in rbac-export-{{quarter}}.json, create a certification row in the Recert portal (tools/recert-portal). Fields to present: principal_email, role_name, resource_scope, last_seen, linked_approver, a link to audit-slice for context, and a precomputed risk score.
- App owners should confirm: still needed, reduce scope, or revoke. Approvals are recorded and the evidence package is versioned (SHA256).

Escalation and exceptions
- If app owner does not respond in 7 days, auto-escalate to manager and SRE lead.
- Exceptions lasting >30 days require documented compensating controls and an owner in JIRA with SLA.
- Emergency revoke: security-ops can revoke binding immediately via platform API and must record the request_id and reason in the incident tracker.

Validation and auditor package
- Package contents for auditors:
  - rbac-export-{{quarter}}.json (signed)
  - active-principals.csv (signed)
  - audit-slice-{{quarter}}.ndjson (signed, with start/end hash manifest)
  - recertification-approvals.csv (export of portal state)
  - evidence-manifest.json (SHA256 hashes for each file)
- Signatures: use a dedicated compliance key in KMS. Store signature objects alongside evidence files.

Post-run checks (T plus 2 days)
- Verify SIEM ingestion: sample 10 audit events from the slice and run the triage queries above; results must match local audit-slice.
- Verify evidence immutability: check S3 object lock or equivalent for the evidence folder.
- Spot audit: Compliance picks 10 random bindings to verify owner justification in PRD or Confluence.

Operational snippets and quick commands
- Export RBAC via API:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLATFORM_TOKEN" "https://platform.api.redwood/v2/rbac/export?since=2024-10-01&until=2024-12-31" -o rbac-export.json
- Audit log slice via ES (pseudo):
  curl -s -XGET "https://es-internal/_search?scroll=1m" -d '@audit-slice-query.json' | jq -c '.hits.hits[]._source' > audit-slice.ndjson
- Compute evidence manifest SHA256:
  for f in *; do sha256sum "$f" >> evidence-manifest.sha256; done

Known pain points / gotchas
- RBAC v2 stores some legacy bindings under the old namespace; the export script must map legacy.role -> role_name to avoid double-counting.
- SIEM enrichment (people-service calls) can fail under load; fallback: attach principal_email only and mark enrichment_failed flag.
- Some service accounts are managed by infra teams and should be exempt from owner-driven revocation; ensure exemptions are included in the exemption list (exemptions.yml in repo infra/compliance).

Open questions (for next design iteration)
- Should we make the recert portal “owner auto-assigned” using Git metadata (owner in infra repo) when app owner is missing?
- How strict should automated revocation be for unused keys older than 90 days if owner is unknown? (risk vs breakage)
- Can SIEM enrichment be batched to avoid people-service throttling? (proposal: periodic HR export to an internal lookup table)

Appendix: useful links and artifacts
- Confluence: RBAC v2 design and role taxonomy (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- GitHub: access-evidence-snap tool (github.com/redwood-inference/access-evidence-snap)
- JIRA epic: JIRA-SEC-987 (quarterly automation)

Notes to self (informal)
- Diego: double-check that tools/compute-role-delta.rb handles wildcard scopes.
- Priya: patch SIEM pipeline to tag event.action if outcome!=success so auditors can filter failures easily.
- Samir: schedule a dry-run two weeks before the quarter to verify all pipelines.
- Keep a short demo deck for execs showing time-to-certify improvements after automation.

Revision history:
- 2024-10-12 created by Ava Chen (initial draft)
- 2024-11-02 updates: added SIEM field mapping and sample queries (Diego)
- 2025-01-10 updates: tightened evidence signing guidance and added escalation SLA notes (Priya)

End of document.
